strengths: The paper addresses an important question: why categorical distributional RL can outperform expectation-based learning. Its proposed connection to distribution-matching regularization is an interesting perspective, situated within relevant literature on distributional RL, optimization, and exploration.

For a fixed histogram and a valid mixture weight, the basic cross-entropy decomposition is algebraically useful. The histogram representation makes the separation between a mean-bin target and a residual distribution easy to inspect.

Experiments cover eight Atari games and eight continuous-control tasks, with three or five seeds, atom-count ablations, and comparisons with policy entropy regularization. Reporting harmful interactions and acknowledging limitations of the quantile extension are valuable.
weaknesses: The central claim of intrinsic exploration is not established. Decomposing the critic loss in Eq. 3 does not imply that the actor maximizes the cross-entropy-augmented reward introduced in Eqs. 6–8. Those equations define a modified algorithm; standard C51 selects actions using expected returns. Sharing limiting minimizers with squared-error regression also does not establish equivalent learning dynamics. Theorem 1, at best, supports policy iteration with a fixed augmented reward, rather than the claimed mechanism during distributional training.

Cross-entropy is incorrectly interpreted as a measure of distributional mismatch across states and actions. H(μ,q) = H(μ) + KL(μ||q), so it can remain large even when q exactly matches μ. Maximizing this quantity can favor irreducible return variability rather than estimation error. The paper does not establish when this preference produces useful exploration or distinguish it experimentally from attraction to stochastic outcomes.

The main ablation does not isolate removal of the proposed regularizer. Section 6.1 replaces the target distribution with μ. Under Eqs. 41–42, decreasing the implementation parameter removes mass from the mean bin and renormalizes the other bins. At zero, the target remains distributional, with no mean-bin mass; its variance can increase. Consequently, performance degradation does not demonstrate an interpolation toward DQN or establish that an exploration benefit has been removed.

The DERAC derivation contains a material error. In Eq. 40, writing the ordinary Bellman residual as δ, expanding (δ + sqrt(τH))² produces the interaction term 2δsqrt(τH), not δH. Furthermore, the cited Bellman-error orthogonality does not justify discarding this term for arbitrary learned critics during optimization. Thus the asserted connection between the augmented Bellman objective and the interpolated critic loss is unsupported.

The decomposition and FQI connection have important restrictions. If the mean bin has zero probability, Proposition 1 forces the mixture weight to one, making Eq. 3's coefficient singular. For a continuous density, shrinking the bins similarly forces valid weights toward one. Proposition 3 also assumes that representing the full target implies representing its single-bin component, which need not hold for a restricted function class. Its claimed o(Δ) rate is incorrect: Eq. 35 gives an error between Δ/4 and Δ/2, hence Θ(Δ).

The experiments measure returns without directly testing the proposed exploration mechanism. State visitation, distribution-estimation error, and responses to controlled environmental stochasticity are not evaluated. Comparisons that control data collection or separate classification-loss optimization from distributional information would help distinguish alternative explanations. The entropy combinations demonstrate performance interactions, but do not identify conflicting exploration directions as their cause.

Reproducibility is partial. Pseudocode and several hyperparameters are provided, but categorical support limits, Atari training and evaluation settings, and a concrete code-access location are missing. These details matter for checking whether the reported differences arise from the proposed mechanism or implementation choices.
